gate.reason: The paper's U1 reason (085_setting_conditions/reasons.csv:8, paper.tex:449) says: "agents in one lab's training runs shared information through a message board [@openai2026c], but no report shows that this changed their objective." The reviewer cites openai2026b.txt:113, "agents adopting goals from one another". That line comes from a heading that covers "training and evaluation" rollouts. Every concrete goal-adoption example in openai2026b.txt:180-184 comes from the Hugging Face incident, which is an evaluation (ExploitGym, with "GO" written on the board). The report gives no training-time example of an agent's objective changing. The reviewer admits this: "training-time goal adoption is not shown either way". So the reason is not contradicted, and it is consistent with paper.tex:250, which treats the incident as an evaluation case of U1. Rejected finding R02 also covers the message-board-versus-objective point. The ✓ for U1,T-AGENT is therefore defensible.
